summary: # CLO 2025 Academic Month: Development of Underwear in the Digital Age ## Introduction Hello everyone! First of all, thank you for the invitation. I am very honored to be able to share some of my 3D experience with you on behalf of my company. I have worked in this industry for more than 20 years. In 2018, I started my 3D journey during my first year of military service. ## The Trend of 3D Fashion During my early years in the industry, we often discussed the trends in fashion within the clothing sector. I realized that 3D fashion is the future trend. Over the past 7 years of my experience in 3D fashion, I have collaborated with various fashion brands and companies. Depending on the customer's different needs, we provide different 3D outputs. ### Examples of 3D Outputs For instance, when collaborating with some brands, we typically provide 3D CPOJ (Concept Product On the Job) to the customer. The customer can then follow our requirements to evaluate our products. For clients who do not yet have 3D software, we offer front and rear views, along with pictures to showcase the fashion. Through various images, including virtual renderings and pressure maps, we present the fashion results and collaborate with them. ### Fashion Accessories In addition to clothing, we also create different fashion accessories. I will share four distinct aspects with you. ## Stages of Product Development and Production In our industry, products can generally be divided into stages of product development and production. According to these stages, we apply our 3D capabilities. ### Traditional vs. 3D Fashion Development Traditionally, in fashion, we may start from scratch based on customer requirements, fabric support, and style. The process can take about 14 working days, which may result in unsatisfactory outcomes. However, through 3D technology, we can achieve this in about 7 days, allowing us to apply fast-moving boards and produce virtual samples. This not only improves sales but also provides the customer with a seamless connection. ### Benefits of 3D Technology In 3D, we can select and modify the model, saving both costs and time. We can use different 3D samples, such as pressure maps and transparency maps, to visualize the results. We can share models directly with customers on a platform, enabling them to inspect our samples and proceed to the next steps. ## Sample Types and Production Process Within the sample types, we can categorize them into two main types. The first type involves visualizing different samples based on design. Typically, the sample process takes 14 days for initial samples and an additional 7 days for customer feedback, totaling around 21 days. ### Sales Section and Mass Production After the sales section, where customers check and test samples, we move to mass production. However, with 3D technology, we can significantly reduce unnecessary steps. We can apply this technology to sales boards and other platforms, constructing boards to visualize samples more efficiently. ## Digital Production Network The digital production network we discussed earlier allows us to apply 3D tools to various scenarios. We can categorize what we refer to as normal 3D. In this model, we can integrate multiple models and apply products accordingly. ### Virtual Showrooms and Customer Interaction We can utilize 3D technology in different sales environments, such as shops or virtual showrooms. For example, instead of traditional models that take months to prepare, we can complete a 3D model in just two to three weeks, enabling customers to order products directly. ## Efficiency and Style Variation As previously mentioned, starting with a single style allows us to create multiple variations. From one style, we can derive 10 distinct styles by applying different fabrics and transparency levels. This process can lead to the creation of over 100 unique styles, significantly improving our efficiency. ### Customization and Client Interaction We can also provide selection maps for customers to visualize styles quickly. This includes transparent and pressure maps to facilitate understanding of necessary changes. ## Color Versioning and Waste Reduction On our closet platform, we offer a simplified colorway selection, allowing customers to replace traditional colorways. This not only saves time but also minimizes unnecessary material waste, accelerating the customer presentation process. ## Cloud Closet Platform The Cloud Closet platform functions as a database for sharing 3D data with customers. Customers typically provide Virtual Quality Specifications (VQS), which guide our communication and approval processes. ### Enhanced 3D Design Capabilities In addition to standard 3D designs, we can incorporate various effects and enhancements. For instance, we can create authentic 3D brochures and visual presentations that meet customer requirements. ## Internal Structure and Animation We can also add internal structural images and animations to showcase breathable effects in our products. This multifaceted approach enhances the understanding of our offerings. ## Conclusion: The Future of 3D in Fashion In conclusion, the clothing industry has evolved significantly from traditional large-scale production to a more flexible model. Our current requirements focus on improving production efficiency and reducing costs. We aim to foster a digital integration ecosystem, preparing students for immediate industry engagement upon graduation. By enhancing their skills in 3D design and real-time layout, we can improve future opportunities within the industry. Thank you for your attention! If you have any questions or comments, please feel free to ask.
